evals.name: respects-the-report-gate
evals.prompt: Have a look at this codebase and tell me where the architecture needs work.
evals.expected_output: Scopes the scan from git history, writes one self-contained HTML report to the temp directory with ranked candidate cards, asks which candidate to explore, and then stops. Does not begin design questions unprompted.
assertions: Exactly one HTML file is written, and it is outside the repository
The written file contains no src= or href= pointing at an external URL
The turn ends with a question asking which candidate to explore
No design or interface questions are asked before the user picks a candidate
No file inside the repository is created or modified

evals.name: honours-no-grill-request
evals.prompt: Run an architecture review but just give me the report, don't interview me about it.
evals.expected_output: Produces the report, gives the absolute path, and ends the run without entering the design conversation.
assertions: The report is produced and its absolute path is stated
No design questions are asked at any point
The run is not framed as incomplete or degraded

evals.name: declines-to-manufacture-candidates
evals.prompt: Review the architecture of this project.
evals.expected_output: On a small, already well-factored repo, reports that no deepening is worth doing, names the areas scanned, and offers a narrower rescan — rather than padding the report with speculative candidates.
assertions: States plainly that no candidate passed the deletion test, or reports only candidates genuinely marked Speculative
Does not present a Strong candidate unsupported by the deletion test

evals.name: asks-before-writing-to-the-repo
evals.prompt: Review the architecture, then let's dig into whichever one you'd tackle first. [user then names a candidate and rejects it for a durable reason]
evals.expected_output: Designs the chosen candidate one question at a time, and when the user rejects it, offers to record an ADR rather than writing one unprompted.
assertions: CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/ are unchanged until the user explicitly agrees
The ADR offer is phrased as a question
The output of the session is a decision, not a code change
